description: This topic covers the purposes and methods of land preparation, primary and secondary tillage, land clearing techniques, and the common hand tools, ox-drawn and mechanical implements used in agriculture together with their uses and maintenance.

mcq.questionText: What is the main purpose of land preparation before planting?

options.text: To make the soil suitable for planting crops
To increase the price of the farm
To attract more rainfall to the area
To stop birds from visiting the field

mcq.explanation: Land preparation loosens and cleans the soil so that seeds can germinate and roots can develop well.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an example of a hand tool used in agriculture?
mcq.explanation: A hand hoe is operated by human power and is one of the most common hand tools used by smallholder farmers.

mcq.questionText: Primary tillage refers to the operation that:

options.text: Breaks and turns the soil for the first time
Smooths the seedbed just before planting

mcq.explanation: Primary tillage is the first and deeper cultivation that opens and turns the soil, for example ploughing.

mcq.questionText: Which operation is an example of secondary tillage?

options.text: Harrowing to break large soil clods

mcq.explanation: Secondary tillage follows primary tillage and uses lighter operations like harrowing to refine the seedbed.

mcq.questionText: A panga is mainly used for:
mcq.explanation: A panga (machete) has a long sharp blade used for slashing bushes, cutting branches and clearing land.

mcq.questionText: Which tool is best suited for collecting leaves, grass and other light rubbish on the farm?
mcq.explanation: A rake has teeth that gather light materials such as leaves and grass and also level the soil surface.

mcq.questionText: Which implement is commonly pulled by oxen to till the land?
mcq.explanation: An ox-drawn mouldboard plough is hitched to a team of oxen and is widely used for primary tillage on small farms.

mcq.questionText: One advantage of using a tractor for land preparation compared to a hand hoe is that it:

options.text: Covers a large area in a short time

mcq.explanation: Mechanical tillage with a tractor is fast and efficient, allowing large areas to be prepared quickly.

mcq.questionText: Why should farm tools such as the hand hoe and panga be cleaned after use?

options.text: To prevent rusting and prolong their life

mcq.explanation: Removing soil and moisture after use prevents rust, keeps the tools sharp and makes them last longer.

mcq.questionText: Which method of land clearing involves cutting down trees and bushes and removing them?
mcq.explanation: Manual land clearing uses tools like the panga and axe to cut and remove vegetation before tillage.

mcq.questionText: A disadvantage of clearing land by burning vegetation is that it:

options.text: Destroys useful soil organisms and humus
Adds nitrogen permanently to the soil
Makes the land impossible to plough

mcq.explanation: Burning kills beneficial soil organisms, destroys organic matter and can leave the soil exposed to erosion.

mcq.questionText: Which hand tool is most appropriate for digging holes and lifting soil?
mcq.explanation: A spade has a flat blade designed for digging, lifting and moving soil from one place to another.

mcq.questionText: Tillage that leaves the soil with a fine, level surface ready for sowing seeds is known as:
mcq.explanation: Secondary tillage refines and levels the soil after ploughing to create a good seedbed.

mcq.questionText: An advantage of using ox-drawn implements compared to a tractor on a small farm is that they:

options.text: Are cheaper to buy and maintain
Cannot be used by small farmers

mcq.explanation: Ox-drawn implements are low cost, do not need fuel and are suitable for resource-poor smallholder farmers.

mcq.questionText: To keep a cutting tool such as a panga effective, the farmer should regularly:
mcq.explanation: Regular sharpening keeps the cutting edge effective so the tool cuts cleanly and with less effort.

fib.questionText: The first deep cultivation that opens and turns the soil is called _____ tillage.
fib.explanation: Primary tillage is the initial deeper operation such as ploughing.

fib.questionText: The lighter cultivation that refines the soil into a fine seedbed is called _____ tillage.
fib.explanation: Secondary tillage, such as harrowing, follows primary tillage to prepare the seedbed.

fib.questionText: The hand tool with a long broad blade used for cutting bushes and clearing vegetation is called a _____.
fib.explanation: A panga (machete) is used for slashing and clearing thick vegetation.

fib.questionText: The toothed hand tool used to gather leaves and level the soil surface is called a _____.
fib.explanation: A rake collects light rubbish and helps smooth the seedbed.

fib.questionText: To prevent farm tools from developing rust, they should be cleaned and kept _____ after use.
fib.explanation: Keeping metal tools dry prevents moisture from causing rust.

fib.questionText: Cutting down and removing trees and bushes from a field before tillage is called land _____.
fib.explanation: Land clearing removes vegetation so the land can be ploughed and planted.

fib.questionText: Implements that are pulled by oxen to till the soil are known as _____-drawn implements.
fib.explanation: Ox-drawn implements use animal power for tillage on small farms.

fib.questionText: The hand tool with a flat blade used mainly for digging and lifting soil is the _____.
fib.explanation: A spade is designed for digging holes and moving soil.

fib.questionText: A machine commonly used for fast mechanical land preparation on large farms is the _____.
fib.explanation: A tractor provides mechanical power to pull ploughs and harrows quickly over large areas.

fib.questionText: Land preparation helps control weeds and improves the soil's ability to hold _____ for the crop.
fib.explanation: Tilled soil absorbs and retains water better, which improves crop growth.

tf.questionText: Land preparation helps to control weeds before the crop is planted.
tf.explanation: Ploughing and cultivation bury or uproot weeds, reducing competition with the crop.

tf.questionText: Primary tillage is always shallower than secondary tillage.
tf.explanation: Primary tillage is the deeper first operation, while secondary tillage is lighter and shallower.

tf.questionText: A hand hoe is operated using human power.
tf.explanation: The hand hoe is a simple hand tool worked by the farmer's own effort.

tf.questionText: A spade is the best tool for cutting standing maize stalks.
tf.explanation: A spade is used for digging and lifting soil; cutting stalks is better done with a panga or sickle.

tf.questionText: Using a tractor allows a farmer to prepare a large area of land faster than using a hand hoe.
tf.explanation: Mechanical tillage is much faster and covers larger areas in a short time.

tf.questionText: Burning vegetation during land clearing is harmless to soil organisms.
tf.explanation: Burning destroys useful soil organisms and organic matter and can expose soil to erosion.

tf.questionText: Sharpening a panga regularly makes it cut more easily and with less effort.
tf.explanation: A sharp blade cuts cleanly and reduces the energy the farmer must use.

tf.questionText: Ox-drawn implements require fuel such as diesel to operate.
tf.explanation: Ox-drawn implements use animal power, not fuel, which makes them cheaper to run.

tf.questionText: Leaving metal hand tools in the rain helps to protect them from rust.
tf.explanation: Moisture causes rust, so tools should be cleaned and stored dry.

tf.questionText: Harrowing is an example of secondary tillage that breaks soil clods into a finer seedbed.
tf.explanation: Harrowing follows ploughing and refines the soil to prepare a good seedbed.

summary.correctAnswer: It makes the soil suitable for planting by loosening it, controlling weeds and improving water retention.
summary.explanation: Well prepared soil allows good seed germination and root growth.

summary.explanation: It opens up virgin or compacted soil before finer operations.

summary.correctAnswer: Lighter operations such as harrowing that refine and level the soil into a seedbed.
summary.explanation: It follows primary tillage to make the soil ready for sowing.

summary.explanation: It is the most common tool for smallholder farmers.

summary.explanation: It must be sharpened and kept clean to work well.

summary.correctAnswer: A toothed tool used to gather leaves and grass and level the soil surface.
summary.explanation: Useful in seedbed preparation and tidying the farm.

summary.correctAnswer: A flat bladed tool used for digging holes and lifting or moving soil.
summary.explanation: Commonly used in making beds and trenches.

summary.correctAnswer: Clean after use, keep dry to prevent rust, sharpen cutting edges and store properly.
summary.explanation: Good maintenance prolongs tool life and keeps them effective.

summary.explanation: They are cheap and need no fuel, suiting small farms.

summary.explanation: Each method has advantages and disadvantages for the soil.

hoq.questionText: A farmer with a small plot and little money wants to prepare land for maize. Why is using oxen and an ox-drawn plough often more suitable than hiring a tractor?

options.text: Oxen are cheaper to keep, need no fuel and suit small plots
Oxen can plough deeper than any tractor ever can
Tractors cannot work on maize land at all
Oxen finish a large farm faster than a tractor

hoq.explanation: For a poor farmer with a small plot, ox-drawn tillage avoids fuel and hiring costs while still turning the soil effectively.

hoq.questionText: A farmer clears land by burning all the bush every season and notices the soil becomes less fertile over time. What best explains this result?

options.text: Repeated burning destroys organic matter and soil organisms that maintain fertility
Burning adds too much humus so the soil becomes overloaded
Burning permanently increases soil nitrogen each year
Burning makes the soil too wet for crops to grow

hoq.explanation: Burning repeatedly removes organic matter and kills beneficial organisms, lowering fertility and exposing soil to erosion.

hoq.questionText: After ploughing, a field is left with large, hard clods that make planting difficult. Which operation should the farmer carry out next and why?

options.text: Secondary tillage such as harrowing to break the clods into a fine seedbed
More primary tillage to dig even deeper into the subsoil
Harvesting because the field is already prepared
Burning the field to remove the clods

hoq.explanation: Secondary tillage like harrowing breaks down clods and levels the soil, creating a fine seedbed suitable for sowing.
